mac_setup_notes:
Hardware: Apple M5 Max, 64 GB unified memory, 2 TB SSD, macOS high-power mode on AC (methodology.md:155-162). Per apple.com/macbook-pro/specs, the 64 GB option exists only on the 40-core-GPU M5 Max, so the bandwidth is 614 GB/s (the 32-core part is 460 GB/s and ships with 36 GB only). This laptop: 896/614 = 1.46x the bandwidth, for weights that fit fully in VRAM (estimate). Engine: Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0 through the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint at temperature 0 and top_p 1 by default (measured-profiles.json measuredAgainst). Ollama's per-model params (temperature 1, top_p 0.95 and so on) are therefore overridden by the request. Dates: 22-23 Aug 2026. Database: the embedded SQLite sample only. Method: six surfaces, five consecutive passes each. A pass needs goal verdict `answered`; the timings are whole-run wall-clock (several turns plus tool calls), not tok/s, and are taken as best case on a rested machine. Losses during a 3.5 h sweep were thermal and were re-measured. Engine version matters: gemma4:12b went 5/5 on 0.32.13 to 1/5 on 0.33.0 with the same digest (methodology.md:164-179). Context: no num_ctx or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is recorded for these five models; only qwen3.6 states OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768. The prompts are small (SQLite schema), so the runs say nothing about 64k-context behaviour. Per-turn limit: 90 s shipped, 150 s for nemotron-3-nano:30b, nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b and glm-4.7-flash:latest. nemotron3:33b and gpt-oss:20b stay at 90 s. Shipped settings, from src/lib/agent/model-tuning/measured-profiles.json:
- nemotron3:33b: retryUnreadStop, refusalExamples, thinking on.
- nemotron-3-nano:30b: turnTimeoutMs 150000 only, thinking on.
- nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b: turnTimeoutMs 150000 only, thinking on.
- glm-4.7-flash:latest: suppressPlanReasoning (plan turn think off), reportReminderLimit 2, retryUnreadStop, turnTimeoutMs 150000. Agent-side suppression was tried and made optimize worse (0/3).
- gpt-oss:20b: suppressAgentReasoning on all five agent surfaces, perWorkflow query-optimization temperature 0.8 and top_p 0.9, retryUnreadStop.
A 10-model UI sweep (57/60) did not necessarily include these models; everything else is over HTTP.

models.underlying_model: OpenAI gpt-oss-20b, 21B / 3.6B active MoE, MXFP4 (HF openai/gpt-oss-20b; ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF)
models.mac_result: 30/30 (measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio). Median run 37 s, slowest 2:49. Per surface: Investigate 19 s, Optimize 78 s, Assess 142 s, Operate 30 s, Analyze 31 s, Plan 16 s. Turn limit is the shipped 90 s. Settings: reasoning suppressed on all agent turns (without it, 4 of 6 surfaces lost runs to turns spent thinking), plus query-optimization at temperature 0.8 / top_p 0.9, because at 0 it rewrote the statement identically and the plan comparison was refused. retryUnreadStop is also set. The assess cell once read 1/5 on an older build. Ollama 0.32.13/0.33.0. Disk on the page: 13 GB.
models.kb_status: Top 10, rank 9 (docs/model-selection.md:53, 185-199): the required gpt-oss member and pipeline baseline, with the caveat 'weak independent agentic scores' (AA TB2.1 13.9, NVIDIA TB2.1 15.17). The only model measured on this laptop.
models.ollama_tag_facts: gpt-oss:20b = latest, digest f38aa0c53da5. Model blob 13,793,422,816 B (12.85 GiB), file_type MXFP4, 20.9B, requires Ollama 0.30.0. Library page: 14GB, 128K context, Text input, badges tools / thinking / cloud. Params: temperature 1. The Harmony template emits 'Reasoning: <level>' when think is set with a level, 'Reasoning: medium' when unset or true, and no Reasoning line when think=false. Sources: https://ollama.com/library/gpt-oss/tags and https://registry.ollama.ai/v2/library/gpt-oss/manifests/20b.
models.fit_detail: llama.cpp, measured on this laptop: ggml-org MXFP4 (11.28 GiB file) at -c 131072 with q8_0 KV uses 13,360 MiB of GPU memory, 166 tok/s decode, tool call and OpenCode session passed. Ollama tag (estimate): 12.85 GiB weights plus 64k KV in f16 (12 full-attention layers x 24 KiB/token = 1.5 GiB, plus under 0.1 GiB sliding) plus about 0.5-1 GiB compute/CUDA = about 14.9-15.4 GiB against 15.47 GiB, so tight. OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 with OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 gives about 14.2-14.6 GiB. OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 is required, since the default here is 4k. System RAM need: about 2-3 GiB.
models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with the KB recipe (measured: -c 131072, q8_0 KV, -fa on, --jinja, GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1). It is faster than vLLM (83.5 tok/s, eager only) and has more headroom than the larger Ollama blob. To mirror the harness's 'no agent reasoning', use reasoning_effort low on llama.cpp. On Ollama the equivalent is think=false, which drops the Reasoning line rather than setting low. That mapping is not verified to behave the same. Ollama 0.33.0 is the fallback only to replicate the harness exactly.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Faster (estimate). The model fits fully, so decode is bandwidth-bound: 896 vs 614 GB/s = about 1.46x. The measured 166 tok/s here is about 87% of the bandwidth ceiling. Prefill on the RTX should be well ahead too (7.4k tok/s at 8k, measured here). The harness's whole-run times (37 s median) should shrink here, but not by a fixed factor, because the runs are tool-bound and turn-bound.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools: yes (Harmony parser in llama.cpp, tool_choice required enforced, OpenCode write/read session passed here). Thinking: always on; effort low/medium/high. Context: 128k fits on llama.cpp. libredb evidence: 30/30 in a real multi-tool agent loop, but only with reasoning suppressed and a per-workflow sampling override. The default temperature-0, reasoning-on configuration did NOT pass, so OpenCode should run it at low effort. Known open issue: llama.cpp #30781 (HTTP 500 on array params without items).
models.reason: Already rank 9 and measured here. The libredb harness adds first-hand evidence that its tool calling is reliable in an agent loop at low or no reasoning, which partly offsets the weak AA and NVIDIA agentic scores. Its slow assess cell (142 s median) and the need for a sampling override on one surface show it is still weaker than the 30B-class models.

models.fit_detail: KV is tiny: 6 attention layers x 2 x 2 KV heads x 128 x 2 B = 6 KiB/token, so 64k = 384 MiB and 128k = 768 MiB in f16, plus a small Mamba state (estimate). Ollama tag: 23.68 GiB weights, of which about 13.5-14 GiB of whole layers go on the GPU (about 59%) and about 9.5-10 GiB on the CPU. RAM need about 12 GiB (estimate). llama.cpp KB recipe: Q4_0 17.60 GiB with --n-cpu-moe 16, about 15.2 GiB GPU at 128k and about 4.7 GiB of experts in RAM (estimate from the KB).
models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp b12407 with the KB recipe (Q4_0, --n-cpu-moe 16, -c 131072, --jinja, GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1). Only routed experts go to the CPU, and attention, Mamba and shared weights stay on the GPU. That is better than Ollama's whole-layer split, which would put about 40% of all layers, Mamba and attention included, on DDR5. Ollama 0.33.0 with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 is the fallback to reproduce the harness's exact build. Whether Ollama uses the MTP draft on CUDA is unknown.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Slower than the Mac on Ollama, roughly similar to slower on llama.cpp (estimate). On the Mac all 23.7 GiB sit in 614 GB/s unified memory. Here the offloaded part runs at DDR5-6400 dual channel (102.4 GB/s peak, about 60-70 effective), and prefill on CPU-resident layers is the larger penalty. KB estimate for the llama.cpp split: 60-110 tok/s decode (docs/community-benchmarks.md:207). Run times also depend on think length: plan took 144 s on the Mac at a 150 s cap, so a slower machine will hit any per-turn wall sooner.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools: yes (Qwen3-Coder XML format, nemotron_h_moe arch in llama.cpp). Thinking: toggle. Context: 128k-256k on the llama.cpp recipe. NVIDIA lists OpenCode among its training harnesses (KB facts record). libredb evidence: 30/30 with thinking ON and no tool-related overrides, the cleanest tool-reliability record of the three 30B Nemotrons here. Its only weakness is long thinking on planning-style turns, so for OpenCode start with thinking off and enable it per task, as the KB rule says.
models.reason: The KB already holds a recipe for it. It passed the user's six-surface agent harness 30/30 with no behavioural overrides, only a longer turn. That is stronger first-hand tool-reliability evidence than the KB holds for Bolt (rank 7, vendor-run scores only, AA TB 4.0 at 0). On this laptop it is the next model to measure after gpt-oss-20b in this lane.

With 64k f16 KV and about 1 GiB overhead, about 11 GiB of layers fit on the GPU (about 62%) and about 6.7 GiB go to RAM; with q8_0 KV, about 12.5 GiB on the GPU (estimate). models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp b12407 with the KB recipe (--n-cpu-moe 20, -c 65536, --jinja), with thinking off by default. The harness shows its thinking can run until the wall on planning turns. llama.cpp keeps attention and MLA on the GPU and moves only experts, which matters because the KV is large. Ollama 0.33.0 with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 and q8_0 KV is the harness-faithful fallback.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Slower (estimate). It spills here, while on the Mac all 17.7 GiB sit at 614 GB/s. Prefill of the offloaded part on DDR5 is the main penalty for long OpenCode prompts.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools: yes (glm-4.7 parser in Ollama; llama.cpp ships a tested GLM-4.7-Flash template). Thinking: toggle. Context: 198K max; 64k is the practical setting here because of the KV size. libredb evidence: 30/30, with two caveats that transfer. First, thinking runs away on planning turns, so default thinking off. Second, it tends to ask the user for input instead of reading. That is harmless in OpenCode, where a user exists, but it stalls unattended runs. The harness ran it at temperature 0; the KB recipe uses 0.7.
models.reason: Honorable mention with a recipe. The harness confirms reliable tool calling in an agent loop, but it needed three behavioural settings to get there. Its large KV squeezes the GPU budget at 64k, and on this laptop it gives no speed advantage over Lightning, which needed only a longer turn.

kb_implications: gpt-oss-20b (rank 9): add the libredb result as first-hand agent-loop evidence: 30/30 on six tool surfaces (measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio). It sits beside the weak AA and NVIDIA agentic scores and qualifies the 'weak independent agentic scores' caveat. Record that the pass needed reasoning suppressed on agent turns and a per-workflow temperature of 0.8 / top_p 0.9 on query optimization. The KB says thinking 'cannot be turned off'. On Ollama, think=false removes the 'Reasoning:' line from the Harmony system prompt (verified in the registry template), which is not the same as llama.cpp --reasoning-effort low. docs/opencode.md:171 should say this mapping differs by runtime and is untested here.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (honorable, 'fallback if Bolt does not fit'): it is the only Nemotron with first-hand agent-harness evidence (30/30, cleanest overrides, Investigate 4 s on the Mac). Bolt (rank 7) has vendor-run scores only and AA TB 4.0 0. Re-judge the Bolt vs Lightning order with this evidence, or at least make Lightning the first Nemotron to measure here. Its KB llama.cpp recipe (Q4_0, --n-cpu-moe 16) is the right runtime. Add the harness caveat that it spends whatever turn budget it gets: the plan median went from 67 to 144 s when the cap went from 90 to 150 s.

GLM-4.7-Flash (honorable): the harness confirms tool reliability (30/30) and adds an operational rule the KB recipe lacks. Thinking runs away on planning-style turns (0/5, all at the 90 s wall with no output), while blanket agent-side thinking-off made optimize worse (0/3). The llamacpp/models.md GLM entry should default thinking off and note that thinking per task helps some agent turns. Also note its tendency to ask the user for input instead of reading.

Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B: the KB has it only in a discovery record as superseded. Add it to the exclusions table with the reason 'superseded by Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (same footprint, faster and stronger)', and record that it passes the libredb agent harness 30/30. The exclusion is not about tool reliability.

Missing candidate: nemotron3:33b is NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B-A3B Reasoning (released 2026-04-28, vision and audio). It is absent from research/2026-11-15/discovery/models-nvidia.json and model-selection.md. Add it as an evaluated candidate: the text GGUF is nemotron_h_moe (supported at b12407), ggml-org Q4_K_M 20.88 GiB, and the harness passes 30/30 with optimize marginal. Suggested verdict: excluded or honorable as 'same footprint as Lightning plus encoders; only if multimodal input is needed'.

Ollama evidence and version pinning: the harness used Ollama 0.32.13/0.33.0, and its methodology shows a cell flipping from 5/5 to 1/5 between those versions with the same digest. The KB cites Ollama v0.40.16 behaviour and has not pinned an ollama/ollama image. Any Ollama runs meant to reproduce libredb evidence should pin ollama/ollama:0.33.0 (tag exists on Docker Hub, as do 0.32.13 and 0.40.16) and record the model digest.

Ollama tag drift: nemotron3:33b and nemotron-3-nano:30b were re-pushed about 4 weeks ago and nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b about 1 month ago, after the 22-23 Aug 2026 measurements. A pull today may not be the measured build. glm-4.7-flash (5 months) and gpt-oss:20b (1 month, size unchanged at 13.79 GB) are less of a concern; the KB should say the harness evidence is tied to the August digests.

Sampling transfer: the harness ran every model at temperature 0 and top_p 1 (except gpt-oss optimize), while the KB recipes use model-card sampling (temperature 1.0, or 0.7 for GLM tools). Pass rates may not transfer across that difference; note it next to any harness citation.

Coverage gap in this lane: the harness covers rank 9 (gpt-oss-20b) and two honorable mentions, but not Bolt (rank 7). It also covers two NVIDIA models the KB had not ranked.
